stories.name: Thomas Lemaire et al.
stories.story_summary: Volcanologist and heritage researcher at DiSTAR, University of Naples Federico II, who used an Insta360 X4 camera to capture a complete 360° photographic survey of the 1858 lava flow field and lava tubes at Somma-Vesuvius, creating an immersive virtual geoheritage tour hosted on Momento360. The project — published February 2026 in the Springer Nature journal Geoheritage — explicitly names the Insta360 X4 in the methods section and credits Insta360 Studio software for editing and export. Co-authors include Daniele Morgavi, Paola Petrosino, Sonia Calvari, Leopoldo Repola, Diego Di Martire, and Ettore Valente.
stories.why_it_matters: A volcanologist using an Insta360 X4 to build a virtual tour inside the actual lava tubes of Vesuvius is a cinematic story — dangerous terrain, historical significance, and cutting-edge geoheritage technology in one image. The project bridges fieldwork and public education, with the completed tour live and publicly accessible on Momento360. Springer Nature peer-reviewed publication adds strong credibility.
stories.source_quote: 360° photos were captured using an Insta360 X4 camera. The photos were edited and exported within the Insta360 Studio software and hosted on Momento360.
stories.source_type: Peer-reviewed academic journal (Geoheritage, Springer Nature, Volume 18, Article 41, February 2026). DOI: 10.1007/s12371-025-01247-6

stories.name: Francesca Galasso & Rolando Volzone
stories.story_summary: Heritage documentation researchers from the University of Pavia (Galasso, Dept. of Civil Engineering and Architecture) and ISCTE-IUL Lisbon / NOVA IEM (Volzone) who used an Insta360 X3 panoramic camera to conduct a 360° video survey of a difficult-to-access convent cloister at Montemor-o-Novo, Portugal. The project was presented at the CIPA 30th Symposium in Seoul (August 25–29, 2025) and published in the ISPRS Archives (Volume XLVIII-M-9-2025, pp. 511–518). The Insta360 X3 was used specifically for outdoor heritage documentation of the partially ruined, inaccessible cloister.
stories.why_it_matters: Heritage professionals using an Insta360 X3 to survey physically inaccessible historic architecture — a decaying convent cloister — is a compelling use case for the camera's portability and 360° coverage in constrained field conditions. Presented at the world's premier heritage photogrammetry conference (CIPA), it represents professional-level endorsement of the Insta360 X3 for cultural heritage work.
stories.source_quote: video-based acquisition activities in the outdoor environment through Insta360 X3 panoramic camera were conducted in a heritage context
stories.source_type: Peer-reviewed conference proceedings (ISPRS Archives, Volume XLVIII-M-9-2025, CIPA 30th Symposium, Seoul, August 2025). DOI: 10.5194/isprs-archives-XLVIII-M-9-2025-511-2025

stories.name: Osama Jamil & AnnMarie Brennan
stories.location: Melbourne, Australia (University of Melbourne, Melbourne School of Design)
stories.story_summary: Architectural heritage researchers at the Melbourne School of Design, University of Melbourne, who used an Insta360 ONE RS 1-Inch 360 camera to capture a heritage cottage in both interior and exterior, then applied Gaussian Splatting (a cutting-edge 3D generative AI technique) to create immersive virtual models of the building. Their paper — published February 28, 2025 in Frontiers in Computer Science — investigates how Gaussian Splatting changes the visual aesthetic and digital atmosphere of architectural heritage representation. The Insta360 was used in both sunny and overcast conditions to analyze how lighting affects the 3D model.
stories.why_it_matters: The intersection of Insta360 and Gaussian Splatting (a buzzy, cutting-edge AI visualization technique) is a story with strong appeal to Insta360's tech-forward creator audience. The University of Melbourne researchers are using the Insta360 ONE RS as the capture device for next-generation AI-generated architectural heritage models — positioning Insta360 as the camera of choice for cutting-edge spatial computing research. Open-access Frontiers publication makes this verifiable and shareable.
stories.source_quote: The framework for capturing the Cottage begins with video recording using an Insta360 ONE RS 1-Inch 360 camera, divided into two stages: the interior (entrance and chambers) and the exterior.
stories.source_type: Peer-reviewed academic journal (Frontiers in Computer Science, DOI: 10.3389/fcomp.2025.1515609, published February 28, 2025)
